findings.title: SonicWall Security Advisory SNWLID-2024-0015: SonicOS Improper Access Control Vulnerability (CVE-2024-40766)
findings.summary_md: The vendor advisory, first published August 22, 2024, discloses an improper access control flaw (CWE-284, CVSS 9.3) in SonicOS management access and SSLVPN affecting Gen 5, Gen 6, and Gen 7 devices on 7.0.1-5035 and older. A September 6, 2024 revision added that the vulnerability is potentially being exploited in the wild, and November 2024 revisions added threat actor IPs including 88.119.175.104, 45.149.172.51, 172.86.116.8, 216.146.25.208, 194.48.154.67, 162.120.71.224, and 45.61.157.15. Fixed builds are 5.9.2.14-13o for Gen 5, 6.5.4.15.116n (6.5.2.8-2n for SM9800, NSsp 12400, NSsp 12800) for Gen 6, and anything above 7.0.1-5035 for Gen 7; EoL units such as NSA 2600 get no patch.

findings.title: Arctic Wolf Observes Akira Ransomware Campaign Targeting SonicWall SSLVPN Accounts
findings.summary_md: Arctic Wolf reported on September 6, 2024 that Akira affiliates were compromising local SSLVPN accounts on SonicWall devices as their initial access vector, with MFA disabled on every compromised account and vulnerable SonicOS firmware on every affected device. The bulletin repeats SonicWall's fixed-version table and recommends upgrading firmware, resetting locally managed SSLVPN passwords, and enabling MFA. It notes the advisory had expanded that same day to cover both management access and SSLVPN with exploitation language.

findings.title: CISA adds CVE-2024-40766 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
findings.summary_md: The KEV feed records CVE-2024-40766 (SonicWall SonicOS Improper Access Control Vulnerability) with dateAdded 2024-09-09, a required-action due date of 2024-09-30, and knownRansomwareCampaignUse set to Known. The entry cites the SonicWall advisory SNWLID-2024-0015 and a SonicWall notice on Gen 7 and newer firewall SSLVPN recent threat activity.

findings.title: Arctic Wolf Labs Observes Increased Fog and Akira Ransomware Activity Linked to SonicWall SSL VPN
findings.summary_md: Arctic Wolf Labs documented at least 30 Fog and Akira intrusions since early August 2024, about 75 percent Akira, each involving SonicWall SSL VPN, with no affected device patched against CVE-2024-40766. Time from initial SSL VPN access to encryption ran as short as 1.5 to 2 hours, SSL VPN often sat on default port 4433, and firewall telemetry showed login events with message event ID 238 or 1080 followed by 1079, originating from VPS ASNs such as AS64236 and AS32613. The post also provides IOCs including .akira and .flocked extensions, akira_readme.txt, and source IPs like 77.247.126.158 and 208.115.232.194.

findings.title: #StopRansomware: Akira Ransomware, advisory AA24-109A revised November 13, 2025
findings.summary_md: The joint FBI, CISA, and partner advisory was updated November 13, 2025 to state that Akira threat actors likely abused CVE-2024-40766 for initial access and to list it among the CVEs observed for entry alongside CVE-2023-27532 and CVE-2024-40711 in Veeam. It attributes approximately $244.17 million in claimed ransomware proceeds to Akira as of late September 2025 and documents TTPs including 1.5 to 2 hour access-to-exfiltration intervals, the itadm account, SharpDomainSpray password spraying, and Akira_v2 encryptor extensions .akiranew and .aki.
